turns.text: Hey Lloyd, my laptop fan is screaming again. Can you help me troubleshoot?
Hi Alan. That sounds frustrating. First, let's check if any heavy processes are running in the background. Try opening your Task Manager or Activity Monitor.
Already checked. Just Chrome and some code editors. It gets loud when I run local models.
That makes sense given the compute load. You might want to check for dust buildup or consider a cooling pad. Did you clean it recently?
Not lately. I'll get to it this weekend. Anyway, I was reading up on the UK Number 10 Data Science team for that article I'm writing.
Oh, interesting topic. They are quite prominent in government tech. What have you found so far?
The recruitment stats are wild. The team has a highly selective recruitment process with a 0.7% acceptance rate.
Wow, that is extremely competitive. It explains why their output is so high quality.
Right? It's like applying to Ivy League but for public sector coding. Anyway, back to the fan...
Lloyd, did my order for the new mechanical keyboard switches arrive yet?
Let me check your tracking info. Ah, yes, the package was marked delivered yesterday. Check your porch or neighbor's mailbox?
Found it! Thanks. I'm excited to try out the tactile bump. Speaking of structures, I'm still digging into how that UK team works.
The UK Number 10 Data Science team? What aspect are you looking at now?
Their operational model. It's fascinating. The UK Number 10 Data Science team operates as an 'insurgent unit' deploying AI and engineering talent directly into government departments.
That's a unique approach. Instead of building central services, they embed people directly into the ministries. It helps bridge the gap between policy and execution.
Exactly. It's not just consultants handing over reports. They stay in the room. Makes sense why it's so effective.
Indeed. It allows for iterative development within the government context rather than a big bang delivery.
Yep. Okay, I'm going to install these switches now. Wish me luck.
